intro.title: Build SSE endpoint for live updates
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoint in Node.js to stream live updates from a server to a client in real-time. You will learn how SSE enables one-way, persistent connections for sending continuous data, like notifications or live feeds, using plain HTTP. The core programming concepts involve setting up an Express server, handling HTTP headers for SSE, and writing data in a specific event stream format. You'll use key Node.js constructs such as HTTP response objects, event emitters, and interval timers to simulate and send updates. By the end, you'll have a working endpoint that clients can connect to for receiving live data streams.
intro.usecase: SSE endpoints are essential for real-time features in modern web applications. You'll see them powering live dashboards like stock trading platforms or server monitoring tools that update metrics without page refreshes. Social media feeds use SSE to push new posts and notifications instantly to users. News websites implement SSE for live scoreboards and breaking news alerts that appear automatically. As a Node.js developer, you'll build these endpoints to create responsive, data-driven experiences that keep users engaged with current information.
